builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
summary: The benchmark replaces ad hoc or proxy evaluations of LLM agents' system-understanding ability with a reproducible pin-level circuit reconstruction testbed of 18 tasks with hidden stateful references. Adopting it costs simulation infrastructure, agent API spend across many trials, and gate-level netlist verification expertise, none of which serves typical ML production work. Its results show current agents rarely succeed (roughly 12-15% full pass rates) and almost never improve efficiency, so any workflow assuming agents can autonomously reverse-engineer or optimize hardware would fail.
rationale: This is an evaluation benchmark for agentic hardware reverse engineering, not a deployable technique, so it does not address inference, training, or agent-orchestration needs of the reader's production stack.
technique: Black-box circuit reconstruction benchmark for LLM agents

claims.statement: The benchmark replaces ad hoc or proxy evaluations of LLM agents' system-understanding ability with a reproducible pin-level circuit reconstruction testbed of 18 tasks with hidden stateful references. Adopting it costs simulation infrastructure, agent API spend across many trials, and gate-level netlist verification expertise, none of which serves typical ML production work. Its results show current agents rarely succeed (roughly 12-15% full pass rates) and almost never improve efficiency, so any workflow assuming agents can autonomously reverse-engineer or optimize hardware would fail.

Only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials fully passed; function guidance raised mean functional score from 24.6% to 30.9%; only 3 of 58 passing designs improved on the reference's power, area, and delay.
